spec_doc: docs/specs/gig-runs-once.red-spec.json — engine half of the two-repo fix; the store half (coltrane_drain_renew / coltrane_drain_release, attempts/max_attempts, terminal-status guard on the header upsert, lease clearing on terminal writes, manifest merge) lands in eir-labs/coltrane-ui branch work/gig-runs-once and deploys first. CONTRACT SURFACE the laws pin — src/lease.ts: export const HOSTED_LEASE_MS = 60 * 60 * 1000; export const DRAIN_LEASE_ROUTES = { renew: '/rest/v1/rpc/coltrane_drain_renew', release: '/rest/v1/rpc/coltrane_drain_release' }; renew: POST ${COLTRANE_DRAIN_URL}${DRAIN_LEASE_ROUTES.renew} body {p_gig_id} ONLY, Bearer drain key (the route fills p_token), X-Coltrane-Instance (the route fills p_instance); 200 -> new lease_until; 403 / 42501 -> lease lost; release: POST ${COLTRANE_DRAIN_URL}${DRAIN_LEASE_ROUTES.release} body {p_gig_id, p_reason, p_terminal} ONLY, instance in X-Coltrane-Instance -> boolean; WorkOnceDeps.scheduleHeartbeat: (intervalMs: number, beat: () => Promise<unknown>) => () => void; default arms an unref'd setInterval; interval = HOSTED_LEASE_MS / 3; WorkOnceResult.acknowledged: boolean on a claimed result: true iff the store acknowledged the terminal header; terminal header attempts: 3; header status: 'running' is a new GigHeaderRecord status, sent awaited before the first chair with the run's genome_hash; manifest.cold_run_reason: string on a header written by a run that went cold because a resume was refused. ROUND 2: output drains are acknowledged (3 attempts) before the completed header; a 'running' header refused with 23514 or 403/42501 aborts the run with no terminal write. ROUND 3 (branch work/gig-runs-once-r3): G1 the heartbeat stays armed until the terminal header is acknowledged or exhausted; G2 no release after the outcome is decided when the terminal header is unacknowledged; REFUND a non-terminal release only before the first chair invocation; Q6 the drain deadline ends a gig aborted/timeout (WorkOnceResult status 'aborted', aborted:{reason:'timeout'}, header status 'aborted', no gig_fail); G4 (terminal rows only; founder ruling, Eugene: "what's closed is closed. can refer to the sealed outputs on input if needed but reopening doesn't smell right."): the successful resume path at gig_dispatch(resume_gig_id) / `coltrane dispatch --resume` runs today under the OLD id (gigId = resumeArg ?? randomUUID()), which the store's terminal guard answers with 23514; a resume of a failed/aborted gig must dispatch a NEW gig carrying resumes:<old id>, take the old seals as inputs by reference (content_sha in input_shas, never re-sealed), and write nothing under the old id. The refused-resume case is covered by tests/resume_reuse_dispatch.test.ts:164. A parked → approved → re-claimed gig is not terminal and keeps its id (E6b records a cold run there). G4 hosted: the store's claim carries resumes:<old id|null>; workOnce runs under the claim's own id, takes the closed gig's drained seals (coltrane_mcp_gig_outputs for the old id) as inputs by reference, invokes no chair already sealed there, and writes nothing under the old id. The gig_dispatch resume law covers both terminal endings, failed and aborted. ROUND 4 (branch work/gig-runs-once-r4, on the implementation at 16b00dc): WorkOnceResult.status vocabulary is complete | failed | awaiting_approval | aborted | abandoned — `abandoned` = the lease was lost (a refused renew, or a start header refused with 23514 / 403-42501): the worker writes nothing terminal, no gig_fail, no release, and acknowledged:false; it is NOT a failure of the gig and NOT an outcome the store should record from this worker. L1 a late answer after a lost lease is never sealed; E7c a stale holder of a requeued local row is refused; Q6r the aborted header carries manifest.abort_reason = "timeout" as a field; L4 with a store present (ServerDeps.gigStatus → coltrane_mcp_gig_status) the store decides whether a gig is closed for G4. (G4b/G4h cite their laws at 5993cff on work/gig-runs-once-r3; they arrive on this line with the implementer's merge of 4ed5ef4.) ROUND 5 (on 30183e1): R5.1 a resumed gig re-claimed on a fresh box rebuilds from the closed gig's seals AND its own; R5.2 a store that throws or never answers (30 s) refuses the resume — never a checkpoint fallback; R5.3 the closed set is failed|aborted|completed|cancelled, the open set running|queued|awaiting_approval; R5.4 rpcGigStatus (coltrane_mcp_gig_status → status) drives the decision. OBLIGATION OUTSIDE THIS REPO: the HOST (eir-labs/coltrane-ui) must wire ServerDeps.gigStatus = rpcGigStatus(...) the way it wires queueGig — until it does, no hosted door has a store to ask and the checkpoint decides. This is a coltrane-ui follow-up after #554 publishes. ROUND 6 (RED at 2d4e7ab): the HOSTED gig_dispatch branch (createToolSurface → callSurfaceTool, deps.queueGig) must make the same closed-gig decision as the local door: H1 a closed gig's resume queues resumes:<old id> (never resume_gig_id); H2 an open gig's resume is refused (in-place resume is gig_approve's job); H3 a store that throws, never answers (30 s) or is not wired refuses, nothing queued; H4 queueGig receives ONLY the host contract (standard_slug, mode, input, org_slug, acting_for, venue, resumes — what postgrestQueueGig/rpcQueueGig read, plus resumes) and every other advertised gig_dispatch argument (chart_slug, repo_url, depth, effort, max_context_tokens, budget, reuse, approvals, approved_by, wait:true) is refused BY NAME. Budget carriage (a store column) and the coltrane-ui adapter's mapping of `resumes` are the coltrane-ui follow-up. ROUND 6b (review 5326196799 at 2d4e7ab): the fixture now enforces the live store's gig-token scope (status: own gig; outputs: own + the gig the row resumes; else 403/42501) and the drain service's real refusal shape ({error}, no code; 401/403/400 by message) — G4h and R5.1 are therefore RED AT HEAD, as found live. D1 a resuming gig never re-pays for the closed gig's seals under the real scope (fix: the store widens the resume exception to gig_status, or the engine reads the closed gig's genome hash from somewhere its token may read, e.g. the claim); D2 player mode's run timeout stays under its 30-minute lease (the player path has no renew RPC, so it is the timeout, not a heartbeat); D3 ANY non-2xx on the start header (400 without a code, 403, a persistent 503) stops the run before the first chair; S2–S4 book the review's surviving plants. Not booked (review finding 5, low): output-drain state is per process; the CLI is one gig per process. D1 RESOLVED BY THE STORE (conductor): the fixture now mirrors the coltrane-ui follow-up scope (status + outputs readable for exactly the resumed gig), under which G4h, R5.1 and D1 pass at 2d4e7ab; they stay dependent on that follow-up deploying before #554's hosted resume is live. D3-503 requires E2's retries (3 attempts) on the start header before the run stops.

testing_method: vitest, example-based and behavioural: every engine law drives workOnce (or runCli / openLocalQueue) through a stubbed global fetch that plays both hosts — the org store (ctx.baseUrl RPCs) and the drain service (COLTRANE_DRAIN_URL: header, outputs, storage, renew, release) — statefully, so a re-claim reads what the first worker's acknowledged writes left behind. The heartbeat's clock is injected (WorkOnceDeps.scheduleHeartbeat) and fired from inside the chair invocation; acknowledgement is observed by holding the store's answer back (a delayed Response) and asserting what had resolved when workOnce returned. E8 moves the lease constant with vi.doMock over src/lease.ts and asserts both derived numbers follow. New symbols are reached by variable specifiers and casts so tsc over tests/ stays clean.
